chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ibn Fuddal, from Abu Jamiilah, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding His Word, the Mighty and High: 'On the Day when there shall be severe affliction,' he said: 'Blessed be the Supreme [Jabbar]!' Then he pointed to his shin and lifted the clothing which covered it, saying: 'And they shall be called upon to make obeisance, but they shall not be able.' He said: 'The people will be silenced, fear will enter them, their eyes will look fixedly, their hearts will reach their throats, their eyes will be in a state of humbleness, and they will be humiliated when they are called upon to make obeisance, although they are sound.'

Muhammad ibn Ali the Compiler of this book says: What he (peace be upon him) meant by his statement 'Blessed be the Supreme!' after which he pointed to his shin and uncovered it, was 'Blessed be the Supreme! He is far above having a shin, Who is such.'

key_terms.تَبَارَكَ الْجَبَّارُ: Blessed be the Supreme / Blessed be the Compeller
key_terms.يَوْمَ يُكَشَّفُ عَنْ سَاقٍ: On the Day when there shall be severe affliction / when a shin shall be uncovered

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'uncovering the shin' in Surah Al-Qalam according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interprets the phrase 'kashf an saq' (uncovering the shin) as a metaphor for the manifestation of Divine Power, explicitly linking it to God's attribute of 'Al-Jabbar' (The Compeller) by pointing to his own shin to signify that the 'Shin' is God Himself. This interpretation highlights the transition from the ease of prostration in worldly life to the inability to do so on Judgment Day, where the disbelievers are struck with awe and humiliation as their claims of sovereignty are nullified by the true Sovereign.
